subject: ClearPath trial success metrics + streaming integration handoff
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Lin <sarah@clearpath.ai>
Cc: Tom Reyes <tom.reyes@clearpath.ai>, ben_carter@redwood.ai, jordan_blake@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 2 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: ClearPath trial success metrics + streaming integration handoff

Hi Sarah — great to meet today. Quick recap and concrete next steps to keep momentum on the evaluation. Attaching a short mutual action plan and a small tech appendix (streaming-route-spec.md) for your engineers.

Summary (post-demo priorities)
- Trial scope: 2-week sandbox evaluation focusing on customer-message classification and automated reply suggestions.
- Success criteria (ClearPath + Redwood):
  - Accuracy: post-processed classification F1 >= 0.86 on your sample set (we'll run the eval suite you provide).
  - Latency: median end-to-end (1–128 token responses) < 200ms in our US region for streaming endpoints; 95th < 400ms.
  - Stability: zero dropped connections during continuous stream of 1k concurrent connections in your ramp test.
  - Cost target: keep inference token spend within the budgeted pilot number (we'll instrument token logs).
- Data handling: model runs in isolated trial environment; we will not persist customer PII beyond logs needed for diagnostics — SOC2 controls available on request.

Immediate asks / owners
- ClearPath: share sanitized sample dataset + security contact (Sarah) by Tue 4/6. (Sarah)
- Redwoods engineering: provide streaming integration spec + example SDK flows by Mon 4/5. (Ben)
- Product/CS: confirm eval metrics and measurement plan; create shared dashboard. (Jordan)

Proposed trial timeline
- Week 0 (4/5): tech handoff, sample data received, API creds provisioned.
- Week 1 (4/6–4/12): integration + smoke tests (streaming + batch routes).
- Week 2 (4/13–4/19): run evaluation harness, tune prompts/quantization, measure success criteria.
- Final review 4/20: acceptance & next steps.

Technical notes (high level)
- Recommended integration: streaming generation for low-latency suggestions (server -> Redwood SSE endpoint /v1/generate/stream). We support SDK helpers for Node/Python and a server-side SDK for reconnect/offset logic.
- Fallback: non-streaming /v1/generate for short batch work.
- Function/tool calling: supported — we can enable a constrained tool sandbox for your routing calls.

Attachments: redwood-mutual-action-plan.xlsx, streaming-route-spec.md

Thanks — I'll loop Ben for the tech doc. Can we lock a 30-min engineer-to-engineer call on Monday?

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai

- Security: our InfoSec will want the SOC2 report and a short data flow diagram; I've copied Tom (engineering lead) and he will loop in our security contact after review.

We can do the engineer-to-engineer call Monday 4/5 at 10:30am PT — does that work for Ben/Marissa?

— Sarah

sarah@clearpath.ai

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Tom Reyes <tom.reyes@clearpath.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: jordan_blake@redwood.ai, soojin_lee@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 5 Apr 2027 08:05:00 -0700
Subject: RE: ClearPath trial success metrics + streaming integration handoff

Hi Tom / team — Ben here (runtime engineering). Quick technical handoff notes and example flows ahead of our 10:30am call. The attached streaming-route-spec.md has the full table, but key points:

1) Auth & creds
- We will provision a per-trial API key scoped to the ClearPath trial. Keys are bearer tokens sent in X-Redwood-Key header.
- Recommended: server-to-server only; do not embed in client apps. We support short-lived session tokens if you need end-user flows.

2) Streaming options
- We support two streaming transports: Server-Sent Events (SSE) at POST /v1/generate/stream (recommended for most HTTP stacks) and WebSocket streams at wss://stream.redwood.ai/v1/ws for bi-directional scenarios.
- For your real-time suggestion path we recommend WebSocket if you need user typing/ack signals; otherwise SSE keeps implementation simple.

3) SDK snippets (Node)
- SSE example:
  const res = await fetch('https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate/stream', {
    method: 'POST',
    headers: { 'X-Redwood-Key': process.env.CLRP_KEY, 'Content-Type': 'application/json' },
    body: JSON.stringify({ model: 'redwood-small-tt', prompt: prompt, max_tokens: 128, stream: true })
  });
  // consume SSE events and assemble tokens

- WebSocket example: wss://stream.redwood.ai/v1/ws?api_key=REDACTED (payloads are JSON frames; we support resume tokens).

4) Prefix/KV cache behavior
- For chat-like sessions we maintain per-session KV cache; we can pin a subset of messages to the KV cache to reduce latency. Cache TTLs are configurable per trial.

5) Tool calling and safety
- Function/tool calling is available; by default tools are sandboxed. If you require network access, that must be explicitly requested and will be run in an allowlisted environment.

6) Metrics & instrumentation
- We will provide token-level logging, per-request latency, and per-route error breakdowns to the shared Drive dashboard.

Action items for engineering call
- ClearPath: confirm which transport (SSE vs WS) and provide an engineer contact for integration.
- Redwood: share a short smoke-test script + Postman collection to validate endpoints.

Attachments: streaming-route-spec.md

Looking forward to the call — I can walk through reconnect/resume behavior and our recommended batching knobs.

— Ben
Ben Carter
Senior Director, Runtime Engineering, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.ai

From: Tom Reyes <tom.reyes@clearpath.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 6 Apr 2027 09:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: ClearPath trial success metrics + streaming integration handoff

Thanks Ben — a couple quick questions before the call:
1) WebSocket vs SSE: our frontend currently prefers WebSocket for duplex control (typing signals). If you support resume tokens and reconnect, WS sounds fine. Can you confirm max concurrent WS connections per trial?
2) KV cache: will prefix caching be deterministic across restarts during the trial (we may spin up short-lived workers)? We need consistent behavior for user session continuity.
3) Tool calling: we need the ability to call an internal lookup function (customer_id -> preferences). Can Redwood sandboxed tools call back to our private API over a secure, allowlisted tunnel, or do we need to push data into the model call?

Also copying eng-team@clearpath.ai so they have visibility.

— Tom
Tom Reyes
Engineering Lead, ClearPath Analytics
tom.reyes@clearpath.ai

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Tom Reyes <tom.reyes@clearpath.ai>, Sarah Lin <sarah@clearpath.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, jordan_blake@redwood.ai, soojin_lee@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 16:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: ClearPath trial success metrics + streaming integration handoff — next steps and owner assignments

Tom / Sarah — thanks for the quick responses. To answer Tom's questions and close the loop:
- WebSocket concurrency: for the trial we can support up to 2,000 concurrent WS connections in the US sandbox. If you need more we can enable burst capacity.
- KV cache: session caches are persisted to the trial namespace; short-lived workers will be able to resume if they present the session_id. We'll include a small client-side helper in the SDK so you can persist session pointers.
- Tool calling: sandboxed tools can call your private API over an allowlisted egress tunnel. InfoSec will need the exact flow; we've asked for your security contact to finalize the tunnel setup.

Final owner assignments and dates
- ClearPath: provide sanitized sample set + security contact by Tue 4/13 — Sarah/Tom
- Redwood Runtime (Ben): deliver smoke-test collection + WS/SSE examples + reconnect tests by Thu 4/15
- Redwood Product (Jordan): create evaluation dashboard and wire HubSpot deal metrics by Fri 4/16
- Both teams: integration demo & first acceptance run on Mon 4/19 10:00am PT (we'll send a calendar invite).

Open items
- Sign and return the mutual action plan (redwood-mutual-action-plan.xlsx). If we get that back this week we can carve the trial tenant and provision scoped keys Friday.

Links: HubSpot deal https://app.hubspot.com/deals/CLRP-2027-042, Drive folder https://drive.google.com/open?id=1a2b3cREDWOODMPP

Thanks — I’ll send the calendar invite and Ben will share the Postman collection shortly after.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai
